blocks.h2: If You Smell Gas, Do This First
blocks.intro: Your safety comes before any repair:

steps.body: Pets too. Leave the door open behind you.
Leave light switches, phones, the garage door opener and the thermostat alone.
Call Nicor Gas or 911 once you're away from the house.
After the utility says it's safe, we'll track down the leak and fix it.

blocks.h2: Signs Your Gas Piping Needs Work

tiles.h3: There's a Faint Odor by the Furnace or Dryer
tiles.body: Even a slight smell near an appliance is worth checking.
The gas company shut off service, and the system needs a repair and a pressure test.

tiles.h3: The Grill or Fire Pit Won't Light
tiles.body: Outdoor lines can be damaged by digging, frost or a mower.

tiles.h3: A Connector Is Kinked or Old
tiles.body: Moving an appliance can damage the flexible line behind it.

bodies: To find a leak, we work through the system with an electronic gas detector and a soap solution on every fitting, then pressure-test the whole line to prove it holds.

The most common culprits in Mokena homes are appliance connectors, fittings near the furnace and water heater, and outdoor lines added later for grills and fire pits. Once the repair is done, we test again so the utility can turn service back on.

blocks.intro: Most gas piping in Mokena went in during the 1990s or later, but it still needs care.

items.body: Grill, fire pit and pool heater lines run through the yard and need to be installed and protected correctly.
Many newer homes use flexible piping (CSST), which needs proper bonding.
Connectors get bent when appliances are moved. A kinked one should be replaced.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: I smell gas. What's the first thing I should do?
items.preview: Get out, then call Nicor Gas or 911.
items.answer: Get everyone out without touching switches or appliances. From outside, call Nicor Gas or 911. Once it's safe, call us to repair the leak.

items.q: Is the gas line my responsibility or the utility's?
items.preview: The utility owns it up to the meter.
items.answer: Nicor Gas is responsible up to and including the meter. Everything after the meter belongs to the homeowner and should be repaired by a licensed plumber.

items.q: My house has yellow flexible gas pipe. Is that safe?
items.preview: It's CSST. It's safe when it's bonded correctly.
items.answer: That's CSST, common in homes built in the last few decades. It's safe when it's installed and bonded to code, and we can check that it is.

items.q: Can you fix a gas line to a backyard grill?
items.answer: Yes. We repair or replace damaged lines to grills, fire pits and patio heaters and test them before use.

items.q: What does gas line repair cost in Mokena?
items.preview: It varies with the leak. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It varies with where the leak is and how much pipe needs replacing. You'll approve a flat-rate price before any repair.
